title: Maximum Ice Cream Bars
summary: Given an array of ice cream bar costs and the number of coins a boy initially has, determine the maximum number of ice cream bars he can buy.
statement: Given an array of ice cream bar costs and the number of coins a boy initially has, determine the maximum number of ice cream bars he can buy. The boy can purchase the ice cream bars in any order, but he must spend his coins to buy as many bars as possible. Solve this problem using counting sort to count the occurrences of each cost and then purchase the cheapest bars first until the boy runs out of coins.
constraints: Each bar may be purchased once and costs a positive integer amount.
Maximize the number bought without spending more than coins.
hints: To maximize a count under one budget, cheaper bars should be chosen first.
Sort costs ascending and purchase until the next cost exceeds remaining coins.
Subtract each affordable cost and increment the count.
If a solution buys a more expensive bar while skipping a cheaper one, swapping them never hurts feasibility; repeated exchanges yield the greedy prefix.
editorial: If a solution buys a more expensive bar while skipping a cheaper one, swapping them never hurts feasibility; repeated exchanges yield the greedy prefix.

tests.explanation: Buying costs 1,1,2,3 uses all seven coins for four bars.
Every bar costs more than the budget, so buy none.
